headline: Abenomics: the yen weakens and Tokyo shares soar
text: Shinzo Abe, whose party won December's election on a promise to end years of falling prices, announced a 10.3 trillion yen stimulus and pressed the Bank of Japan to target 2% inflation. The dollar rose from about 87 yen at the start of January to about 91 at the end. Exporters' shares are leading a rally in Tokyo.
imageCaption: Shinzo Abe, Prime Minister of Japan, 2013

headline: A weaker yen and a building sale lift Sony
text: Japan's new government under Shinzo Abe is pushing for a weaker yen and aggressive monetary easing; the yen fell about 5% against the dollar in January. On 18 January Sony shares jumped after it sold its New York headquarters building. Sony's ADR rose 33% in January.
imageCaption: The Sony Building in the Ginza district, Tokyo

headline: Battery fires ground the 787
text: After a battery fire on an empty Japan Airlines 787 in Boston on 7 January and a battery problem on an ANA flight, the US Federal Aviation Administration grounded the whole 787 fleet on 16 January, the first grounding of an airliner type since the DC-10 in 1979.
imageCaption: The Japan Airlines 787 that suffered a battery fire, at Boston Logan airport, January 2013

headline: Vasella leaves with a golden handshake
text: Daniel Vasella retired as chairman of Novartis in February after 17 years at the top. His departure package, reported at about $78 million including a payment for not working for competitors, caused an uproar in Switzerland weeks before a national vote on executive pay.
imageCaption: Daniel Vasella of Novartis at the World Economic Forum, Davos, January 2013
imageCredit: CC BY-SA 2.0, photo: World Economic Forum

headline: Berkshire and 3G to buy Heinz for 28 billion dollars
text: On 14 February Heinz agreed to be bought by Berkshire Hathaway and the Brazilian investment firm 3G Capital for 72.50 dollars a share in cash, a 20% premium, in a deal valued at 28 billion dollars including debt. It is the largest deal ever in the food industry.
imageCaption: The Heinz plant in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania

headline: Coca-Cola: 16 billion-dollar brands and a stock split
text: Coca-Cola's net operating revenue passed 48 billion dollars in 2012 and operating income was nearly 11 billion; it returned 9.1 billion dollars to shareholders and announced its 51st consecutive annual dividend increase. In July 2012 it split its stock two-for-one, the first split in 16 years. Two Japanese drinks became billion-dollar brands, bringing the total to 16.
imageCaption: Muhtar Kent, Coca-Cola chief executive, 2012 ;;
imageCredit: CC BY-SA 2.0, photo: World Economic Forum from Cologny, Switzerland

headline: China clears the deal; Davis leaves
text: On 16 April China's Ministry of Commerce approved the merger on condition that Glencore Xstrata sells Xstrata's Las Bambas copper project in Peru by mid-2015 and supplies Chinese buyers with at least 900,000 tonnes of copper concentrate a year for eight years. Mick Davis will not join the combined group: Ivan Glasenberg becomes chief executive at completion and Davis receives £4.6m. The merger is due to take effect on 2 May, when each Xstrata share becomes 3.05 Glencore shares.
imageCaption: Ivan Glasenberg (second from left) with Lionel Barber, Boris Johnson and Lakshmi Mittal at the FT Boldness in Business awards, London, March 2013

headline: Kuroda's 'bazooka': the Bank of Japan doubles the money supply
text: On 4 April the Bank of Japan, under its new governor Haruhiko Kuroda, said it will double the monetary base in two years, buying 60 to 70 trillion yen of bonds a year, to reach 2% inflation. The dollar ended April at about 97 yen.
imageCaption: Haruhiko Kuroda, governor of the Bank of Japan from March 2013
imageCredit: CC BY 2.0, photo: Asian Development Bank

headline: Gold breaks down
text: Gold averaged 1,488 dollars in April, 7 percent below March and 16 percent below its peak month of September 2011. US inflation is only 1.5 percent (March), and shares are at records. The fear of inflation from the Fed's bond buying has not come true.
imageCaption: A one-ounce gold bar

headline: Tesla says it will make its first profit
text: On 31 March Tesla announced that it delivered more than 4,750 Model S cars in the first quarter, beating its target of 4,500, and that it now expects to be profitable for the quarter for the first time. 'Profitability is what makes a company real. Tesla is here to stay,' said Elon Musk.
source: Tesla 8-K exhibit of 1 April 2013, 'Tesla Model S sales exceed target; profitability guidance amended upward', https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000119312513135229/d514482dex991.htm (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Tesla,_Inc. (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Elon Musk with a Model S at the Tesla factory, Fremont, California

headline: Glencore Xstrata is born
text: The merger took effect on 2 May: Glencore issued 6.16 billion new shares, 3.05 for each Xstrata share, and Xstrata left the stock exchange on 3 May. China approved the deal in April on condition that the Las Bambas copper project in Peru is sold, and Ivan Glasenberg is chief executive of the renamed Glencore Xstrata plc; Mick Davis has left. The group is now one of the world's largest miners as well as its largest commodity trader.
imageCaption: Ivan Glasenberg (second from left) with Lionel Barber, Boris Johnson and Lakshmi Mittal at the FT Boldness in Business awards, London, March 2013

headline: First profit and the government loan repaid
text: Tesla reported its first quarterly profit in its ten-year history on 8 May: 11 million dollars on record revenue of 562 million, with 4,900 cars delivered. It then raised 1 billion dollars from new shares and convertible bonds, and on 22 May repaid its 465 million dollar government loan nine years early, the first carmaker in the programme to do so.
source: Tesla First Quarter 2013 Shareholder Letter, 8 May 2013, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000119312513207910/d532640dex991.htm (read 2026-10-03); The Denver Post, 'Tesla Motors fully repays $465 million federal loan nine years early', 22 May 2013, https://www.denverpost.com/2013/05/22/tesla-motors-fully-repays-465-million-federal-loan-nine-years-early/ (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The Tesla Model S, the car behind Tesla’s first profit

headline: Hedge fund Third Point pushes Sony to split off entertainment
text: On 14 May Dan Loeb's Third Point, which holds more than 6% of Sony, wrote to chief executive Hirai proposing to separate the film and music business from the struggling electronics arm. Sony's shares have risen 96% this year. The ADR gained 23% in May.
imageCaption: Daniel Loeb of the hedge fund Third Point

headline: Bernanke hints at slower bond buying and yields jump
text: On 19 June Fed chairman Ben Bernanke said the Fed could begin slowing its bond purchases, now 85 billion dollars a month, later this year. Shares fell about 4 percent in the next three trading days. Bond yields jumped: the 10-year Treasury averaged 2.3 percent in June, against 1.8 percent in April. Gold averaged 1,343 dollars, 5 percent less than in May.
imageCaption: Fed chairman Ben Bernanke at a press briefing, 2013

headline: Rouhani wins on a promise of 'prudence and hope'
text: Hassan Rouhani, a moderate cleric and former nuclear negotiator, won the presidential election on 14 June with 50.7 percent, just enough to avoid a run-off; turnout was about 73 percent. Supporters celebrated in the streets. He promises to ease the economy's pain and to talk with the world about the nuclear programme. The Tehran Stock Exchange rose to its highest since February.
imageCaption: Hassan Rouhani campaigning in Sari, June 2013

headline: Löscher is ousted; finance chief Joe Kaeser takes over
text: In July Siemens replaced Peter Löscher with its finance chief Joe Kaeser, four years before Löscher's contract was due to end, after late deliveries of ICE high-speed trains and delays at offshore wind projects. Kaeser has worked at Siemens since 1980.
imageCaption: Peter Löscher, Siemens chief executive, at the World Economic Forum, Davos, January 2012

headline: Nokia buys out Siemens from the networks venture
text: Nokia agreed to buy Siemens' half of Nokia Siemens Networks for about 2.2 billion dollars, making the network equipment maker a wholly owned subsidiary. The networks business has provided much of Nokia's income while phones lose money.
imageCaption: Nokia's Karaportti campus in Espoo, Finland

headline: Ballmer will retire
text: On 23 August Microsoft announced that Steve Ballmer will retire as chief executive within twelve months, once a successor is chosen. He has led Microsoft since 2000 and is steering it towards becoming a devices and services company.
imageCaption: Steve Ballmer, Microsoft's chief executive

headline: Microsoft buys Nokia's phone business
text: On 3 September Microsoft agreed to buy Nokia's devices and services business for 3.79 billion euros and to license its patents for 1.65 billion euros, 5.44 billion euros in all, about 7.2 billion dollars. About 32,000 Nokia staff will move to Microsoft. Nokia keeps its networks business, its maps and its patents.
imageCaption: The Nokia Lumia 1020, July 2013

headline: Doug McMillon to become Wal-Mart's chief executive
text: On 25 November Wal-Mart announced that Doug McMillon, head of its international business, will replace Mike Duke as chief executive on 1 February 2014. He will be the company's fifth chief executive.
imageCaption: Doug McMillon ;;

headline: The shale boom
text: US crude output is near 8 million barrels a day, up from about 5.5 million in 2010, as horizontal drilling and hydraulic fracturing (fracking) open up shale formations. US oil imports are falling. Brent still costs about $110 a barrel.
imageCaption: A hydraulic fracturing job in the Bakken oilfield, North Dakota
